HOW MUCH IS A PET SCAN

A PET scan is covered under Advanced Imaging Services. For this PPO plan, the in-network cost is 40% coinsurance after the medical deductible whether performed at an outpatient radiology center or in a hospital outpatient department; out-of-network cost is 50% coinsurance after the deductible, and hospital outpatient PET scans also have a $500 per day maximum payable amount for out-of-network facility services.

Urgent care is covered under this PPO plan. For a freestanding urgent care center, the in-network cost is $5 per visit for both facility and professional services; if urgent care is provided in a hospital outpatient setting, the in-network facility cost is $50 per visit. Out-of-network urgent care is generally 50% coinsurance and subject to the out-of-network deductible, except hospital facility urgent care which is $50 per visit out of network as well.
Can I get a quote for the postpartum check-ups as Pre/Postnatal Visits

Yes. Pre/Postnatal Visits are covered under Pregnancy and Maternity Care. For in-network providers, the cost is No Charge. For out-of-network providers, the cost is 50% coinsurance, and the service is subject to the deductible.

I couldn't find a specific ‚Äúcaregiver benefits‚Äù benefit in the current plan document. The closest related benefits in this plan are Home Health Services, Hospice Program Services, and Palliative Care, which may involve support for the Member and family in certain situations.

For anesthesia, this PPO plan generally covers it based on the place of service. What is my copayment for prescription drugs?

Prescription drug copayments depend on the drug tier and whether it is filled as a 30-day retail, 90-day retail, or 90-day mail order prescription. This HMO plan has a $0 pharmacy deductible. Does the copayment on this benefits for outpatient count towards the allowed amount and then you are responsible for the coinsurance

Yes. For this PPO plan, when an outpatient hospital benefit is listed as a combined cost share such as "$150 per surgery + 20% Coinsurance" or "$100 per visit + 20% Coinsurance," the Member is responsible for both the copayment and the coinsurance for that benefit. The plan document does not explain that the copay is subtracted from the allowed amount before coinsurance is calculated, so I could not confirm that specific calculation method from the current plan document.

HOME HEALTH SERVICES FOR DAILY LIVING

Home health services are covered only for skilled home health services provided by a Participating home health care agency in the home under a written treatment plan approved by a physician. Services that are primarily for help with daily living, custodial care, domiciliary care, or private duty nursing are not covered under this plan.[1][2]
